Class ParquetDictionaryAttribute

Namespace
ParquetNeo.DataModel
Assembly
ParquetNeo.Serialization.dll

How the column of a property is dictionary encoded (every column of a collection or dictionary, but not of the properties of an object inside it, which have their own attributes), instead of Standard. A dictionary stores each distinct value once and the rows refer to it, which pays off when values repeat and is wasted work when they do not.

[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = true)]
public sealed class ParquetDictionaryAttribute : Attribute

Remarks

Use Adaptive on a property that is sometimes unique and sometimes repeated, depending on the data written, so that the writer drops the dictionary when the first values show it is of no use. Typical properties: a reference or order number ("ORD-000123"), a Guid or a name that is nearly unique, a timestamp that is recorded to the millisecond, or a measurement such as a price, a temperature or a sensor reading.

Use Disabled on a property that is known to be unique, such as a primary key or an auto-incremented identifier, or whose values are never repeated by nature, such as a free text comment or a url. Nothing is lost, since a dictionary of unique values is larger than the values themselves.

Leave it out (Standard) for properties that take few distinct values: a country, a status, a currency, a category, a boolean-like flag stored as text, a date without a time, a small quantity.

SizeLimit raises (or lowers) how big the dictionary of the column may grow before the writer gives it up, for a column with few distinct values that are large, such as long descriptions or urls that come again and again.

What is set in the options (ColumnDictionaries) wins over this attribute.

Property Value

SizeLimit

The size, in bytes, the dictionary may reach before the rest of the column is written plain, in place of DictionaryPageSizeLimit. Zero, the default, leaves the limit of the writer. The dictionary and the pages that use it are held in memory until the column is complete, so a big limit costs memory.

public int SizeLimit { get; init; }
